decisions.claim: A JSON `null` payload makes msg.token throw synchronously in the socket data callback and kills the broker
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED against src/agent.ts. JSON.parse("null") does not throw, so null sailed past the try/catch and msg.token threw a TypeError in an event handler — an uncaught exception that takes down the process holding every credential on the machine, triggerable by any local process with five bytes on a world-connectable socket. The parsed root is now required to be a non-null, non-array object. Regression tests drive null, scalars, arrays, {} and non-JSON, and assert the broker still answers afterwards.

decisions.claim: The 30s inactivity timeout stays armed while serve() runs, so a legitimate long operation is destroyed mid-flight
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. There is no traffic on the agent socket during an operation by design — the broker is fetching an entry, waiting on a 30s upstream call, or parked on a tier-2 approval for up to 90s. The socket died at 30s, the caller got nothing, and the broker carried on working for someone who had gone. My own tests missed it because the stub returned instantly. The inactivity timer is now disarmed (setTimeout(0)) the moment a complete request has been read; the absolute deadline is what bounds the connection, and it moved 120s -> 180s because 90s of tier-2 wait plus a 30s upstream call does not fit in 120s. Spec check 25 amended with the reason.

decisions.claim: The 1 MiB cap measures UTF-16 code units, not bytes
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. buf.length on a string counts code units, so ~700k three-byte characters is over 2 MiB on the wire and passes a 1 MiB check. Harmless when the only payload was a hex token; a `call` carries an arbitrary body. Now accumulates Buffers and caps on raw bytes. Test sends 700k three-byte characters and asserts refusal plus broker survival.

decisions.claim: Per-chunk d.toString() corrupts a multi-byte character split across TCP reads
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED, and the worst shape a bug can have: non-ASCII only, and only when the split lands mid-character. The broker would have acted on a request that was not the one sent. Now concatenates Buffers and decodes once over the whole line. Test writes a payload containing multi-byte characters in two writes split mid-character.

decisions.claim: listEntries and settings forward API response objects with no output-field allowlist
decisions.reason: Real and worth doing, but it is a change to what the server may send rather than to what this build introduced — the same fields crossed the same boundary before, in the agent's own process. Recorded for the user as an open item rather than changed under this spec.

decisions.claim: No cancellation propagation or per-agent operation queue after a client disconnects
decisions.reason: Real. An authenticated caller can start expensive work and hang up. Out of scope for this spec, which is about key custody rather than resource control, and the caller is already authenticated — so this is a cost question, not a boundary one. Recorded as an open item.

decisions.claim: recordDestination runs before tier approval and the SSRF check, so a refused request is still recorded as a destination
decisions.reason: Correct about the ordering and wrong about it being a defect — it is deliberate and documented at the call site. A first sighting recorded only on success would alert again on every retry of a tier-2 request the owner had not yet answered. The store records ATTEMPTS, which is what an exposure review needs; recording only deliveries would hide precisely the attempts worth looking at. The reviewer's underlying point — that the store's meaning should be stated — is fair, and the comment already says so.

decisions.claim: Decrypted credentials become immutable JS strings; only the byte buffers are wiped
decisions.reason: True and unfixable in this language. Already recorded as a known limit in the phase-5 handoff for the browser side; the same applies in the broker. Wiping the buffers is worth doing anyway and is done. Noted for the user rather than pretended away.

decisions.claim: My own patch deleted the token check while rewriting the socket handler
decisions.reason: Caught by reading the patched file rather than by a test — the suite still passed, because no test presented a WRONG token to the new dispatch path. Restored, and the gap is now covered: the malformed-input tests assert 'unauthorized' for every shape.
